verdict.rationale: Bento documents two things of its own that support portability. Skills and rules live in your repo as Markdown and YAML. The CLI can do anything the dashboard does, including reading runs and pulling analytics, with raw JSON output you can pipe to a file. Trace ingestion over OpenTelemetry is an import path, not an export, so it is not credited. Missing for 10: a documented bulk or complete data export (traces, runs, issues, signals), an export of traces in an open format such as OTLP, offboarding or account-deletion guidance, and independent or hands-on confirmation that the data can be fully extracted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Skills and rules live in your repo as Markdown and YAML. They're model-agnostic, so when you upgrade your model, your accumulated knowledge transfers automatically.
Anything you can do in the dashboard, you can do from your terminal, a script, or CI: triage issues, read runs, inspect signals, pull analytics.
Plain JSON to stdout. Pipe into `jq`, `grep`, or a file.
